title: Derivatives and Embedded Derivatives
outcomes: Identify derivatives using the three characteristics.
Account for standalone derivatives at fair value.
Decide when embedded derivatives must be separated.

meta.exam_tip: For embedded derivatives, first ask whether the host is a financial asset — if yes, do not split.

concepts.title: What makes a contract a derivative
body: A derivative has three features: its value changes with an underlying variable (interest rate, price, exchange rate, index, credit rating, or a non-financial variable not specific to a party); it needs no initial net investment, or one smaller than for similar contracts; and it is settled at a future date.
Examples: forwards, futures, swaps, options (purchased or written). An option premium is a small initial investment relative to buying the underlying, so options are still derivatives.
Contracts to buy or sell non-financial items are derivatives only if net-settleable and not held for own use.
concepts.analogy: Underlying, little upfront money, settlement later — all three make a derivative.
concepts.work: An interest rate swap with nil initial value is a derivative.

concepts.title: Accounting for standalone derivatives
body: Derivatives are financial assets or liabilities at fair value through profit or loss, unless designated as effective hedging instruments.
They are recognised when the entity becomes party to the contract — even if fair value is nil at inception. A forward contract is recognised at nil and gains or losses arise as rates move.
Fair value reflects market inputs (forward rates, volatility, credit risk). Changes in fair value go to profit or loss each period, producing volatility unless hedge accounting is applied.
concepts.analogy: Every derivative is on the balance sheet at fair value.
concepts.work: A forward with favourable rates becomes an asset.

concepts.title: Embedded derivatives: when to separate
body: An embedded derivative sits inside a larger (hybrid) contract and makes some cash flows vary like a standalone derivative. A derivative attached to a contract but separately transferable is a separate instrument.

If the host is a financial asset within Ind AS 109, the whole hybrid is classified as a unit (usually failing SPPI → FVTPL). For other hosts, the embedded derivative is separated when: its economic characteristics and risks are not closely related to the host; a separate instrument with the same terms would be a derivative; and the hybrid is not measured at FVTPL.

Closely related examples: inflation-indexed lease payments, caps and floors out of the money at inception, foreign currency in a functional or commonly used currency. Not closely related: equity- or commodity-indexed interest, leveraged features, calls in equity hosts.
concepts.analogy: Split only what behaves differently from the host contract.
concepts.work: A loan whose interest follows a stock index hides an equity derivative.

concepts.title: Common derivative instruments
body: Forward contract: customised agreement to buy or sell at a fixed future price. Futures: standardised exchange-traded forwards with daily margining.

Options: right without obligation to buy (call) or sell (put); the writer receives a premium and bears the obligation. Swaps: exchange of cash flow streams (interest rate swap: fixed for floating; currency swap: principal and interest in different currencies).

Separated embedded derivatives are measured at fair value; the host is accounted for under the relevant standard. If the derivative cannot be measured separately, the whole contract is designated at FVTPL.
concepts.analogy: Know the instrument to know its underlying.
concepts.work: A company paying fixed and receiving floating has swapped its interest exposure.

illustrations.title: A currency forward
illustrations.q: Orbit Ltd. enters into a forward on 1 February to buy USD 10 lakh at ₹83 on 31 May; no premium is paid. It is not designated as a hedge. At 31 March, the forward rate for 31 May is ₹84.5. On 31 May, the spot rate is ₹82. Ignore discounting. Show amounts in profit or loss.

illustrations.title: Separate the embedded derivative?
illustrations.q: Assess separation for Orbit Ltd. (holder or issuer as stated): (a) Orbit issues a bond whose interest is linked to the Nifty index; (b) Orbit issues a loan with an interest rate cap above market rate at issue; (c) Orbit holds a bond whose principal is linked to gold prices; (d) Orbit leases a warehouse with rent indexed to local inflation; (e) Orbit sells goods to a German customer priced in USD (neither party's functional currency, and USD is not commonly used in that market).

solution.title: Embedded derivatives

jobs.title: Derivative register
jobs.situation: Treasury signed forwards and swaps; procurement signed foreign-currency supply contracts.
steps: List all derivatives and fair value them.
Scan commercial contracts for embedded features.
Book changes in profit or loss unless hedging.
jobs.takeaway: Embedded derivatives often hide in ordinary contracts.

mcqs.q: Which is not a feature of a derivative?
mcqs.explain: A large initial investment points away from a derivative. In practice: compare to buying the underlying.
mcqs.topic: What makes a contract a derivative

mcqs.q: Derivatives not designated as hedges are measured at:
options: Fair value through profit or loss
mcqs.explain: Changes hit profit or loss. In practice: hedge accounting can reduce volatility.

mcqs.q: A forward contract with nil fair value at inception is:
mcqs.explain: It is still a contract the entity is party to. In practice: value moves later.

mcqs.q: A hybrid contract with a financial asset host in Ind AS 109 scope is:
mcqs.explain: No bifurcation for asset hosts. In practice: often FVTPL.

mcqs.q: Inflation-indexed lease rentals based on the local economy are:
mcqs.explain: Non-leveraged local inflation is closely related. In practice: no split.

mcqs.q: Interest linked to an equity index in a debt host issued by the entity is:
mcqs.explain: Equity risk differs from debt risk. In practice: fair value the embedded derivative.

options: Receives a premium and bears an obligation
mcqs.explain: Writers take on obligations. In practice: written options are liabilities.

mcqs.q: An interest rate swap typically exchanges:
mcqs.explain: Currency swaps exchange currencies. In practice: used to hedge loans.

model.title: Embedded derivatives

summary: Derivative: underlying, small investment, future settlement.
Recognised even at nil fair value.
Other hosts: separate if not closely related.
traps: Splitting embedded features from financial asset hosts.

viva.q: State the three characteristics of a derivative.
viva.model: Its value changes with an underlying, it requires little or no initial net investment, and it is settled at a future date.
At fair value through profit or loss unless designated as effective hedging instruments.

viva.q: When is an embedded derivative separated?
viva.model: When its risks differ from those of the host (failing the closely related test), would meet the derivative definition alone, and the hybrid is outside FVTPL — and the host is a non-asset contract.

viva.q: Why are financial asset hosts not split?
viva.model: Because Ind AS 109 classifies the whole hybrid asset using the SPPI and business model tests.
Forwards are customised private contracts; futures are standardised, exchange-traded and margined daily.

cases.title: Vector Metals Ltd.
cases.case: Vector Metals Ltd. buys a 2-year call option on 1,000 shares of another company for a premium of ₹50,000. It also has a supply contract to buy coal priced in rupees, settled by physical delivery for its plant, and borrows under a loan whose interest is 2 × MIBOR − 4% (leveraged).

mcqs.explain: Small premium relative to the shares; value follows share price. In practice: remeasure each period.

options: Outside Ind AS 109 under own use
mcqs.explain: Physically settled for usage needs. In practice: no fair valuing.

mcqs.q: The leveraged interest feature in the loan is:
mcqs.explain: Leverage can double rate exposure. In practice: fair value separately.

mcqs.q: Initial carrying amount of the option (₹):
mcqs.explain: The premium paid equals initial fair value. In practice: transaction costs expensed.
